(the holy hour each sunday evening in st mary’s oratory will cease for the moment, resuming after christmas.) readings for 30th sunday in ot 1st reading: it is c.1200 bc. in this passage the lord is teaching his people something never before heard in the religions of the world. as much as the lord cares for us as his beloved creation, he vehemently requires us to care for one another, especially the weakest and most defenceless among us. there is a strict prohibition here against usury between the rich individual and the poor person in need. 2nd reading: this letter is the earliest writ- ing of the new testament. paul compliments his converts from thessaly on having taken to the gospel “with the joy of the holy spirit”, in spite of serious opposition. news of how they had broken with idolatry had already “spread everywhere” (even without the internet!). gospel: in this gospel reading jesus is in jerusalem. before long he will be arrested by the chief priests and elders. he uses their carefully contrived questions to reveal ever more about god and our relationship with him. love of god and of neighbour cannot be separated. ‘herin lies the difference be- tween jesus’ teaching and that of the scribes and pharisees.’ (glenstal bible missal) disney junior club g | 70mins sat 24th 5pm matinee sun 25th 3pm all saints and all souls

ardmore parish | 25 october 2026 ardmore parish newsletter thirtieth sunday in ordinary time 25 october 2026 year a gospel reflection | matthew 22:34 –40 in today’s gospel, jesus teaches that the greatest commandment is to love god who leheartedly and to love our neighbour as ourselves. these two responsibilities are inseparable and form the foundation of christian loving god involves more than religious practices such as prayer, worship, and scripture r eading. it means trusting him in difficult times, remaining faithful through challenges, choosing what is right, and allowing him to guide every aspect of our lives. genuine love for god is shown not only in words but also in daily actions. our love for god becomes visible in how we treat others. we cannot truly love god while harming, judging, or refusing to forgive those around us. instead, we are called to show compassion, kindness, patience, and mercy. even simple acts such as listening, encouraging, forgiving, and helping those in need can become powerful expressions of god’s love. jesus also calls us to recognise the dignity and worth of every person, incl uding those who differ from us or disappoint us. true love does not ignore wrongdoing, but it speaks the truth with respect ands ets boundaries without hatred. the central message of this gospel is that love must be at the heart of both our rel ationship with god and our relationship with others. faith is not measured by religious knowledge or activities alone, but by whet her it transforms us into more loving people. when love guides our thoughts, words, and actions, our lives become a living witness to god’s presence in the world. prayer for the week may the lord bless us with hearts open to love. may he help us to see christ in one another and to bring kindness, hope, and compassion wherever we go. sunday readings | 1 november – all saints first reading: revelation 7:2 –4, 9–14 psalm: 24:1– 2, 3–4, 5–6 second reading: 1 john 3:1 –3 . thank you, from deborah lowry and all at team hope! as our parishes prepare to welcome fr chris next weekend, fr thomas and i take this opportunity to wish him every blessing in his ministry in aghyaran, ardstraw west & castlederg and drumqu in. born in 1986, fr chris is a native of leckpatrick parish. his parents, rosemary and sean , live in strabane. fr chris tells us that his three brothers, two nieces and a nephew form his closest family. following school, chris was employed for several years in an administrative role at the oncology department of altnagelvin hospital. he subsequently pursued seminary studies at st malachy’s college, belfast, and st patrick’s college, maynooth. since ordination in june 2016, fr chris has ministered among the faith communities of st eugene’s cathedral in derry, drumragh (omagh), limavady, kilrea & desertoghill, errigal (garvagh) and granaghan (swatragh). fr chris says that, a fter spending the last five years ‘on the missions’ in co derry, he now looks forward to serving the people of the west tyrone pastoral area. he and kobe (thepet dog) will take up residence in castlederg parochial house at the end of the month. fr chris brings many gifts to his ministry and, in giving generously of himself to serving the people entrusted to his care, i know that he will enjoy the support and encouragem ent of you all. i pray god’s blessing on all that you will share and accomplish together. please keep fr chris in your prayers as he prepares to move to castlede rg and begin the next chapter of his priestly ministry in the west tyrone pastoral area. may god bless you all, fr paul.
